Why Russia Does Not Want Peace – Analysis of the Kremlin’s Latest Statements — Despite the desire of senior US officials to bring Ukraine and Russia to the negotiating table, there are still no signs that Russia seeks peace. On the contrary, an analysis of Vladimir Putin and Sergey Lavrov’s statements clearly indicate that Russia is looking for new ways to escalate the conflict.

The War Is Coming Home to Russians — Russia’s war in Ukraine is beginning to directly affect everyday Russians after years of insulation. Is the war coming home to roost? The evidence suggests it is. Rising casualties may force mobilization in Moscow and St. Petersburg, while Ukrainian drone strikes are crippling refineries, logistics networks and major distributors such as Wildberries. Italy-Led EU Mission Boards Russia-Linked ‘Shadow Fleet’ Tanker in Mediterranean — An Italy-led EU naval mission boarded a sanctioned tanker linked to Russia’s “shadow fleet” in the Mediterranean, the second such operation in under two weeks. The inspection is part of a broader European effort to tighten enforcement of sanctions targeting Moscow’s oil exports.

Baltic Startups Take Aim at Deterring Russia on NATO’s Eastern Flank — Russia’s war in Ukraine has fueled a boom in Baltic defense startups, with companies developing drone and battlefield technologies for Ukraine and NATO allies. Entrepreneurs say the war has accelerated innovation, investment, and military cooperation, strengthening the region’s resilience against growing threats from Russia and Belarus.

Ukraine Strikes Russian Drone Development University, Wildberries Logistics Hub, Crimea in Overnight Raid — Ukrainian drones struck a Russian university reportedly developing drone control systems, a Wildberries logistics hub in Vladimir region, and multiple targets in occupied Crimea overnight, expanding Kyiv’s campaign against Russia’s military and logistics infrastructure.

US to Cede Command of Group Coordinating Military Aid, Training to Ukraine — NATO allies are expected to take over command of the Ukraine Security Assistance Group (SAG-U) as the US scales back its role in Europe. The transition is part of a broader effort to shift responsibility for supporting Ukraine’s military to European partners, while arms deliveries are expected to continue.

Lubomyr Medvid: ‘Ukraine Can Become Europe’s Teacher, Not Its Stepchild’ — For more than six decades, Lubomyr Medvid has explored history, exile, faith and human conscience. In this wartime monologue, he argues that a renewed Ukraine can become Europe’s partner – and even its teacher.

Ukrainian Soldiers’ Homecoming Odyssey — The new cinematic adaptation of Homer’s epic is poignantly relevant to the lives of Ukraine’s warriors, who will need to transcend their war experience. Peace is not merely the absence of a foreign enemy. It requires the restoration of justice.

Ukraine’s Success — Clearly, Trump must learn how to identify enemies and choose allies more wisely. In Ukraine’s case, he finally appears to be heeding the wisdom contained in the 4th-century Sanskrit proverb: “The enemy of my enemies is my friend.”

Belarus Forms New Airborne Brigade Near Ukraine — Belarus has begun forming a new airborne assault brigade in the southern Gomel region, approximately 40 kilometers (25 miles) from the Ukrainian border. SOF Commander Alexander Ilyukevich announced that the 37th Separate Airborne Assault Brigade is actively recruiting, with one battalion already established and additional artillery and support units currently being formed. The new brigade adds to Belarus’s three existing airborne units.

Russian Elites Grow Impatient as Propagandists Panic — Vladimir Putin is facing growing internal pressure as Russian elites, including top banker German Gref and oligarch Andrey Melnichenko, express unprecedented impatience over the failing war and economic ruin caused by Ukrainian drone strikes. Reports indicate elites are moving billions abroad in preparation for a potential mutiny, prompting increased security around Putin’s Valdai residence. Russian Arms Shipment Reaches Mali via Togo — The sanctioned Russian cargo vessel Mikhail Britnev delivered a large shipment of military vehicles to Mali’s ruling junta via the port of Lomé in Togo. The ship, which departed Baltiysk on June 18 and was escorted through the English Channel by a Russian Ropucha-class landing ship, docked in Togo on July 9. Satellite imagery confirmed the vessel was carrying armored personnel carriers and trucks, which were later seen arriving in Bamako on July 25.

Russia’s Cyber War Against the West — Russia is not just waging an aggressive cyber campaign against the West – a campaign that fits a well-established Russian pattern of using cyber operations to undermine Western governments, collect intelligence, and prepare the battlefield. Moscow has also positioned itself as a champion of global cyber rules.

Russia Strikes Kharkiv Postal Terminal, Kills 1 — Russian forces struck a postal terminal in the suburbs of Kharkiv on Sunday, Aug. 2, killing one person and igniting a massive fire that engulfed cargo trucks and equipment. Rescue operations remain ongoing. Later in the morning, Russian forces dropped a FAB-250 guided aerial bomb on Sloviansk in the Donetsk region, destroying a dozen private homes and an administrative building, severely wounding a 61-year-old man.

Russia Strikes Rozetka Hub in Brovary Twice in 24 Hours — Russian forces launched a second drone strike on the main logistics hub of Ukrainian e-commerce company Rozetka in Brovary, Kyiv region, overnight on Aug. 2. Co-founder Iryna Chechotkina confirmed two Shahed drones hit the company’s largest warehouse, though no employees were injured in this second attack. Zelensky Seeks UAE Help to Secure Black Sea Routes — President Volodymyr Zelensky held talks with UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on Aug. 1 to discuss securing Ukrainian maritime routes and global food security. Zelensky noted Ukraine’s past assistance to Gulf partners against Iranian attacks, seeking reciprocal support in the Black Sea. The outreach comes amid heightened tensions with Tehran, following Iranian accusations that Ukraine attacked a commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea.

Leaderless but Unstoppable: Ukraine’s Networked Maidan Redefines Protest Power — Mass protests in the Ukrainian capital, triggered by the resignation of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, continue to ramp up, despite the fact that neither Fedorov nor any other prominent figure serves as a clear organizer. Why is this happening?

Armenian PM Pashinyan Resigns in Procedural Move — Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and his cabinet officially resigned on Sunday, Aug. 2. The move is a constitutional requirement triggered by the convening of the newly elected National Assembly. Pashinyan, whose Civil Contract party won a parliamentary majority in the June 7 elections, is expected to be re-nominated and re-appointed by the president. The June elections endorsed Pashinyan’s strategy to reduce Armenia’s reliance on Russia

Russia Launches 1,900 Drones, 1,600 Bombs in a Week — President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that Russian forces launched approximately 1,900 attack drones, 1,600 guided aerial bombs, and 144 missiles against Ukraine over the past week. The attacks targeted 16 regions and damaged over 1,500 objects, including hundreds of residential buildings. Zelensky called for increased sanctions against the Russian defense industry, which continues to produce these munitions despite existing restrictions.

Boris Johnson Goes ‘Into Ukraine’s Kill Zone’ for New Documentary — Boris Johnson’s new Channel 5 documentary follows the former UK prime minister through Zaporizhzhia as he spends 72 hours near Ukraine’s front line. He meets drone units, witnesses devastation around Komyshuvakha, and argues that the West has grown complacent while Ukrainians fight an existential war, emphasizing they deserve more help.

General Staff Confirms Strikes on Engels Airbase and Saratov Refinery — The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine confirmed that defense forces struck the Engels strategic airfield and the Saratov oil refinery in Russia early Sunday, Aug. 2. The military noted that the Engels base houses Tu-95MS and Tu-160 bombers used to attack Ukraine. Air Defenses Downed 445,000 Russian Targets Since 2022 — Acting Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara stated on Ukraine’s Air Force Day that air defense units have intercepted over 445,000 Russian aerial targets since February 2022, including cruise and ballistic missiles, and drones. Additionally, Ukrainian aviation has conducted over 38,000 combat sorties, destroying more than 12,000 threats. US Pauses Planned Strikes on Iran Amid Deal Talks — US President Donald Trump announced the suspension of a planned 10-to-14-day military campaign against Iran following requests from Tehran and regional states to rapidly negotiate a deal. Trump stated that the agreement must include the immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the cessation of Iran’s nuclear program, noting that Israel supports the pause. Drones Strike Saratov Refinery and Samara Wildberries Hub — Ukrainian drones struck a major oil refinery in Saratov and a Wildberries logistics center in the Samara region early Sunday, Aug. 2. The Saratov strike sparked a large fire, marking the 15th attack on the facility, which previously had operations halted by a July strike. Polish Police Arrest Suspect in Attack on Ukrainian Woman — Police in the Polish city of Gdynia arrested a 76-year-old man on Saturday, Aug. 1, in connection with the July 30 assault on a 40-year-old Ukrainian woman. The suspect allegedly struck the victim twice on the back of the head with a wooden cane before fleeing. The woman was treated for non-life-threatening injuries and discharged. Regional police stated there is currently no evidence linking the attack to national hatred.

Blast at Moscow Restaurant Kills 5 Amid General’s Party — An explosion at the Balzi Rossi restaurant in central Moscow on Saturday evening killed five people and injured 21 others. The Russian National Antiterrorism Committee stated that a woman attempted to carry an improvised explosive device into the venue but was stopped by a security guard; both died in the blast alongside one patron. His words reveal not only one of Ukraine's most influential painters, but also an original philosophical voice whose ideas reach far beyond art.

Latvia Closes Belarus Border — Latvia temporarily suspended border crossings with Belarus on Friday evening due to an information system failure at the Pāternieki checkpoint. Interior Minister Jānis Dombrava urged travelers to use alternative routes. The national cybersecurity agency, CERT.LV, stated there is no indication of a cyberattack or external interference.

The HUR estimated the value of the Pantsir-S1 at $15 million and the Sargan boat at $6 million.

Belarus Designates Polish Press Agency Website ‘Extremist’ — The regime of Belarusian president Alexander Lukashenko has designated the website of Poland’s state-owned news agency, PAP, as “extremist” in a move slammed by leading Belarusian opposition figures.

Trump Threatens Iran With Heavy Strikes on Energy Targets — US President Donald Trump threatened to hit Iran “very hard,” with US media reporting that Washington and Israel are coordinating potential joint strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure, including oil refineries and power plants, as soon as this weekend. In Crimea, Ukrainian forces hit a naval drone storage facility near Chornomorske, the Syvash railway bridge near Chonhar, a railway bridge near Vladyslavivka, a Black Sea Fleet electronic intelligence unit in Sevastopol, and a repair base in Pervomaiske. The Russian Defense Ministry claimed to have intercepted 274 drones across 16 regions. In Ufa, flight operations were restricted as fires broke out at refinery facilities. Due to a critical shortage of Patriot interceptors, Ukrainian air defenses were only able to shoot down one ballistic missile. Explainer: Why Kyiv’s Shelters Fail Civilians Under Russian Attack — Bureaucratic delays, geography and outdated architecture have left Ukraine without enough adequate shelters. Even where protection is available, the realities of a high-intensity war often discourage civilians from using it.

Russian E-Commerce Prices Surge After Wildberries Strikes — Prices for goods on major Russian online marketplaces, primarily Wildberries and Ozon, have surged by 10% to 30% in recent days following a series of Ukrainian drone strikes targeting logistics infrastructure. The price hikes are driven by the sudden cancellation of platform-funded discounts as companies attempt to cover losses and rebuild supply chains. Delivery times have also doubled.

Polish F-16s Intercept Russian Il-20 Plane Over Baltic Sea — Two Polish F-16 fighter jets intercepted a Russian Il-20 reconnaissance aircraft flying over the Baltic Sea approximately 40 kilometers north of Kołobrzeg on July 31. Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz confirmed the aircraft remained in international airspace but was flying without a flight plan and with its transponder deactivated. Zelensky Updates NSDC Roster Amid Government Reshuffle — President Volodymyr Zelensky updated the composition of Ukraine’s National Security and Defense Council (NSDC) on July 31, bringing in new key leadership following a major government reshuffle. The newly appointed members include Commander-in-Chief Mykhailo Drapatyi, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi, and several ministers and acting agency heads, such as Yevhenii Khmara and Andrii Sybiha.

Police are reviewing surveillance footage to identify the suspect, described by witnesses as an elderly man, though a xenophobic motive has not been officially confirmed. The incident has occured amid a documented rise in anti-Ukrainian hostility in Poland, following a recent diplomatic dispute

The Lost Art of Power: From Helmut Kohl’s Resolve to Europe’s Strategic Decay — Europe’s response to Russia’s war in Ukraine reflects a long erosion of strategic will that contrasts sharply with Helmut Kohl’s era of decisive power politics. Pentagon to Hand Ukraine Aid Command to NATO Ally – Politico — The Pentagon plans to transfer leadership of the command coordinating weapons deliveries and training for Ukraine to another NATO member, Politico reported. Officials said the change should not disrupt military assistance.

Toys and Flowers Cover the Ruins as Radushne Mourns Family Killed by Russian Missile — Six of 10 members of the Voronov family were killed when a Russian missile destroyed their home in Radushne on July 30. President Zelensky said preliminary evidence indicated that Russia used a North Korean ballistic missile.

3 Women Hospitalized After Another Russian Drone Strike on Kharkiv — A Russian drone strike on Kharkiv’s Nemyshlianskyi district injured three women aged 41, 47 and 71. The attack followed two earlier drone strikes on the city’s Saltivskyi district.

The Father, the Daughter and the Kremlin: Why Putin Wants Zhanna Nemtsova in Jail — A Moscow court has ordered Zhanna Nemtsova’s arrest over her work with the foundation honoring her murdered father, Boris Nemtsov. The case shows how the Kremlin still fears his democratic legacy and his opposition to Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Fire Breaks Out at St. Basil’s Cathedral on Moscow’s Red Square — A fire broke out in the director’s office at Moscow’s St. Basil’s Cathedral early Saturday, burning an area of about 10 square meters. Around 10 fire engines responded, and the blaze was extinguished without injuries.

9 Killed, 30 Wounded as Russia Pounds Kyiv With Ballistic Missiles — A mass Russian ballistic missile attack killed nine people and wounded 30 across five Kyiv districts. Seven were killed in Darnytskyi, while rescuers evacuated 35 people from a damaged residential building in Solomianskyi.

Trump Casts Doubt on Ukraine Patriot Production License — Donald Trump said Washington has not approved licensed Patriot interceptor production in Ukraine, citing concerns over sharing advanced US weapons technology. His remarks represent a retreat from his July commitment as Kyiv urgently seeks protection from intensifying Russian ballistic missile attacks.
